# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 45

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 10

---

## Disagreement 1 — 45:1 "his lordship" vs. "his dominion"

- **EMET:** "you serve in his lordship"
- **LOGOS:** "you serve in his dominion"
- **PNEUMA:** "you live under his lordship"
- **Greek:** *en tē kyrieia autou* — in his lordship/dominion/sovereignty
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "you serve in his dominion" (LOGOS). *Kyrieia* is the abstract noun of *kyrios*; "dominion" captures the realm-of-authority sense better than the relational "lordship."

---

## Disagreement 2 — 45:1 "made them out of nothing" vs. "established them out of nothing"

- **EMET:** "made all things and made them out of nothing"
- **LOGOS:** "made all things and established them out of nothing"
- **PNEUMA:** "created everything from nothing"
- **Greek:** *epoiēsen ta panta kai ek tou mē ontos eisin* — made all things and they are from non-being
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "made all things and established them out of nothing" (LOGOS). The second verb "established" preserves the two-stage formulation. PNEUMA collapses it into one phrase.

---

## Disagreement 3 — 45:1 "alone is able to contain all things but himself cannot be contained"

- **EMET:** "he alone is able to contain all things but himself cannot be contained"
- **LOGOS:** "he alone contains all things and is himself contained by nothing"
- **PNEUMA:** "He alone holds all things together, and nothing can hold him"
- **Greek:** *monos chorōn ta panta, autos de achorētos ōn* — alone containing/holding all things, being himself uncontainable
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "he alone contains all things and is himself contained by nothing" (LOGOS). The positive/negative formulation preserves the divine infinity argument precisely.

---

## Disagreement 4 — 45:2 "fear him; and fearing him, be self-controlled" vs. "fear him; and in your fear, exercise self-control"

- **EMET:** "fear him; and fearing him, be self-controlled"
- **LOGOS:** "fear him; and in your fear of him, exercise self-control"
- **PNEUMA:** "fear him. Let that fear produce self-control in you"
- **Greek:** *foboū auton; fobou(menos) de autou enkrateuou* — fear him; and fearing him be self-controlled
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "fear him; and in your fear of him, exercise self-control" (LOGOS). The participial construction shows the fear as the basis for self-control.

---

## Disagreement 5 — 45:3 "those who rule over the living and the dead" — interpretation

- **EMET:** "those who rule over the living and the dead"
- **LOGOS:** "those who rule the living and the dead"
- **PNEUMA:** "people with power over the living and the dead"
- **Greek:** *tous kratountas... kai tous nekrous* — those having power over...and the dead
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "those who rule the living and the dead" (LOGOS adjusted). The phrase is preserved without theological gloss; its referent (human or demonic) is left to readers.

---

## Disagreement 6 — 45:3 "delivered up" vs. "given over" vs. "handed over"

- **EMET:** "you will not be delivered up to them"
- **LOGOS:** "you will not be given over to them"
- **PNEUMA:** "you won't be handed over to them"
- **Greek:** *ou paradothēsē autois* — you will not be handed over/delivered to them
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "you will not be given over to them" (LOGOS). All three are acceptable; "given over" carries the passive surrender nuance of *paradidōmi* appropriately.

---

## Disagreement 7 — 45:4 "your commandments are great and good and glorious"

- **EMET:** "your commandments are great and good and glorious"
- **LOGOS:** "your commandments are great and good and glorious"
- **PNEUMA:** "your commandments are great, good, and glorious"
- **Note:** All three agree on the content; only punctuation differs.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "your commandments are great and good and glorious." The triadic *kai...kai* structure of Hermas's Greek is preserved.

---

## Disagreement 8 — 45:4 "very hard toward God" vs. "hardened toward God"

- **EMET:** "the heart of a man is very hard toward God"
- **LOGOS:** "the heart of a man has become very hardened toward God"
- **PNEUMA:** "their heart has grown hard toward God"
- **Greek:** *sklēra ē kardia tou anthrōpou sphodra pros ton theon* — the heart of the man is very hard toward God
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the heart of a man has become very hard toward God" (LOGOS/EMET blend). The perfect tense in LOGOS is appropriate — hardening is a process that has reached a state.

---

## Disagreement 9 — 45:5 "these thoughts are of the devil" vs. "from the devil"

- **EMET:** "these thoughts are of the devil"
- **LOGOS:** "these thoughts are from the devil"
- **PNEUMA:** "those thoughts come from the devil"
- **Greek:** *tou diabolou eisin hai ennoiai autai* — these thoughts are of the devil
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "these thoughts are from the devil" (LOGOS). "From" makes the origin explicit; "of the devil" (EMET) is genitive of possession which LOGOS's "from" better represents in English.

---

## Disagreement 10 — 45:5 "call to mind him who is able to do all things" vs. "think about the One who can do all things"

- **EMET:** "remember rather him who is able to do all things"
- **LOGOS:** "call to mind him who is able to do all things"
- **PNEUMA:** "think about the One who can do all things"
- **Greek:** *mnēsthēti tou dynamenou panta poiēsai* — remember/call to mind the one who is able to do all things
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "call to mind him who is able to do all things" (LOGOS). *Mimnēskomai* is an active remembrance verb; "call to mind" is more active than "remember."

---

*End of disagreement log for Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 45.*
